back: The period when people made and used iron tools; in Zimbabwe divided into the Early (first millennium CE) and Later (from about 1000 CE) Iron Age.
Heating iron ore with charcoal in a clay furnace to separate the iron.
The study of the past through material remains such as pottery, tools, bones and buildings.

front: Name two Early Iron Age traditions in Zimbabwe.
back: Gokomere (near Masvingo) and Ziwa (around Nyanga); also Zhizo in the south-west.

front: Main crops of Early Iron Age farmers?
back: Sorghum, finger millet and pearl millet, with beans and gourds.

front: Which animals did Early Iron Age farmers keep?
Why did iron tools lead to larger villages?
back: Iron hoes and axes cleared and dug land faster, so more food was grown and stored to feed more people.

front: Why are Early Iron Age dates given as ranges?
back: There are no written records; dating methods such as radiocarbon give approximate ranges.
